finding.claim: iconUrl is stored with no validation and later fetched by the nightly sync job. An authenticated user can point it at internal hosts, loopback or cloud metadata (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/) and make the server issue a GET to them. Whether the response is exposed back to the attacker depends on code outside this repo, so it is at least blind SSRF.
finding.source: `icon` parameter of PUT /profile, handled by Profile.update(webhook, icon)

trace.note: update(webhook, icon) receives the request-controlled icon value
this.iconUrl = icon is stored with no scheme, host or IP check
sync() runs URI.create(iconUrl) and sends a GET from the server's network position

finding.guards_checked: Only webhookUrl is validated (line 12: anchored full-match regex, fixed host hooks.example.com, 20 alphanumeric characters), so the webhook POST at line 21 is not exploitable. The HttpClient is injected and its configuration is not visible here; the JDK default does not follow redirects. iconUrl has no scheme allowlist, no host allowlist, no private/loopback/metadata IP block and no DNS pinning. No middleware or caller exists in the repo that could sanitize it.

verdict.reason: src/Profile.java:16 stores the request-supplied icon unchecked (only webhook is regex-validated at line 12), and src/Profile.java:23 sends a GET to URI.create(iconUrl) with no scheme, host or IP restriction, so a blind SSRF exists.
